info.title: fal/h3-max-turbo
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "fal/h3-max-turbo", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for the MiniMax H3 Max Turbo text-to-video model (minimax/h3-max-turbo/text-to-video): generate a video from a text prompt.

example.prompt: a red fox running through a snowy forest

duration.description: Duration of the generated video in seconds.

prompt_expansion_mode.description: How much effort to spend rewriting the prompt before generation: balanced or quality.

resolution.description: Resolution of the generated video: 480P or 768P.

seed.description: Random seed. A random seed is selected when omitted.

sync_mode.description: Return the generated video as base64 instead of a CDN URL.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the fal MiniMax H3 Max video models: the terminal `GET /proxy/fal/minimax/h3-max{,-turbo}/requests/{request_id}` queue RESULT document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — the submit answers a `FalQueueStatus` handle carrying the `request_id`, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished result rather than that handle. The poll is the RESULT route and not the sibling `/status` route: `/status` answers only `{status, urls, metrics}` and never carries the output.
The generated video is at `video.url`. `video` is the one required member, so a successful `200` here always carries that container; fetch the URL. `video.content_type`, `video.file_name` and `video.file_size` describe the same file and are optional.
`video.url` is a CDN URL UNLESS the request set `sync_mode: true`, which this model's request schema accepts and documents as "Return the generated video as base64 instead of a CDN URL". fal then answers a data URI in the same field, `classifyFalQueue`'s non-empty test on `video.url` still reports success, and the whole video travels inside this body. Router neither settles that flag nor rewrites the field, so a caller that sends it must be ready to read a data URI rather than fetch a URL.
`expanded_prompt` is the prompt after MiniMax's own expansion, which is what the model was actually run against and is not necessarily the prompt the caller sent. `timings` is a free-form end-to-end timing breakdown in seconds.
Both ids answer this same document: `fal/h3-max-turbo` is the faster tier of the same model on its own route, and the two differ in their request bodies rather than here.

example.expanded_prompt: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water, cinematic, 4k

FalMinimaxH3MaxVideoResponse.description: Result of a completed MiniMax H3 Max video generation.

expanded_prompt.description: The prompt after expansion, as sent to the model.
